items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: Frank Sinatra is mentioned by the interviewer as part of a playlist of top songs from 1966; the interviewee does not mention any personal interaction or relationship with Sinatra.

ctx.x: Yeah, ’66 I was, yeah, that’s right. Mid-way through college. Yeah.

Yeah. And the playlist top songs of that year included everyone from the Mamas and the Papas, The Beatles, Ray Conniff, The Monkees, and Frank Sinatra. So were you a person who listened to music by this point, noticing things that the average listener did not?

I don’t know. I don’t know what the average listener is listening to, but I mean my interest was not listening for anything in particular, it was just enjoying the music. I started out as a musician playing, you know, through I guess grade school, junior high school, started playing brass instruments, trombone, baritone horn, that sort of thing. Always had an interest in my life that I never really fulfilled totally to my liking of keyboard/piano playing. But the brass instruments, and the trombone in particular,…
